title: Introduces "Candela" mining navigation networks, integrating vents, fultons and mining MODsuits
author: SmArtKar
body: ## About The Pull Request Marker beacons in miner kits have been replaced with brand new "Candela" navigation beacons. (Marker beacons themselves are still available for purchase in the mining vendor to be used as decor) Navigation beacons can connect to each other and other Candela nodes to form a network, linking with nearby vents and extraction beacons. Miners spawn with 30 beacons on their person (instead of 10 marker beacons they got before) and can purchase additional beacons in mining vendors. Beacons can be linked to an existing network by clicking on a node with one, and will automatically place new nodes if you are about to break LoS with the closest node or exit its range when held in your hands or pockets, ***or when placed in your explorer rigging*** (any belt or pocket slot storage works). Using the beacon in-hand will manually place a node and link you to it, and right-click in-hand will sever any connections. An active ore vent connected to the network will power it, causing the beacons to glow brighter and prevent mob respawns in a sizeable area around each node, allowing miners to secure their routes from local fauna. Roundstart ore vent located next to the mining base acts as a "booster" instead, increasing all ore vents' outputs within a network by 33%, incentivizing players to set up infrastructure connecting new vents to their base to boost their rates. --- MODsuits can utilize the new Candela spool module (required advanced mining research) to automatically deploy nodes from their inventory, freeing a user's pocket or webbing slot. Additionally, miners can craft a luminetworked MODsuit core using some beacons and a bluespace crystal, which has rather low capacity but will automatically recharge itself when connected to a powered network. --- Extraction fultons and beacons availible to miners (contractor fultons are untouched) have also been integrated into the network - using a fulton while near an active network lets you teleport to any vent within said network as if it was a beacon. Both fultons and beacons also cost noticeably less. You still can use fultons to teleport back to the station at any point, without a network requirement. This shifts their primary use case from means of getting back to the station from lavaland to a mobility tool, letting miners quickly get back to a vent or their forward base after a storm passes, or escape back to the outpost when caught off guard by one without a capsule. ## Why It's Good For The Game This gives miners an incentive to set up infrastructure, and means to defend themselves from constantly respawning fauna. In the future, once more content is added, we could possibly make the network connection mandatory for vents and remove bluespace boulder teleportation in favor of proper transportation. The changes to fultons should make them more attractive to both new and experienced players, as their current usage as a quick ticket to the station is only useful for corpse retrieval at best, and not worth the points otherwise. I'm hoping to add more engineering content to lavaland in the future using this system as well, making more jobs interact with it rather than relegating it to only 3 people in a round.

changes.text: Added "Candela" navigation networks and beacons, acting as a way for miners to mark their paths, boost vent outputs and protect their routes from fauna respawns
Miners no longer spawn with marker beacons
Mining fultons can now transport miners to tapped ore vents within nearby Candela networks in addition to extraction beacons, and both cost significantly less points
Syndicate extraction beacons can only be reached by syndicate fultons

title: Refactors plane masters/parallax to support non eye perspectives
author: LemonInTheDark
body:
## About The Pull Request

This is something I've wanted to do since planecube.

The goal is to allow popups to display space parallax, and render different z levels properly.

The idea is instead of basing everything off the client's eye, plane master groups and parallax should be based off some sort of like, atom perspective that's placed on the map.

This is simple in concept and kind of annoying as shit in implementation, which is why this is so long.

#### Parallax

Parallax is currently half managed by the hud datum, and passed along between the same client. If we're seperating it from the hud, this cannot continue.

So, parallax becomes a keyed datum stored on JUST /client that's responsible for its own concerns. We can use signals to hook to movement. This also means we get to remove client_mobs_in_contents (which is also just a duplicate of a recursive contents type) and the cruft attached to the parallax subsystem.

It gets a perspective (/atom) var which gets set to either the client's eye or whatever the map view is doing.

We need to use a trait with args for the parallax on/off stuff, because we don't want maps to conflict.

In the process we pull the remaining parallax config vars off /client and onto the datum itself.

#### Plane Masters

The story is basically the same here, plane master groups get a perspective var, different subtypes use it differently (/main maps to client.eye, /popup sets to the map_view's display atom).

There's some extra fiddling in here because we have stuff that expects client.eye to be the perspective var, so that needs to be converted over. Mostly weather code.

I removed offset tracking from hud code (and thus COMSIG_HUD_OFFSET_CHANGED) because it was redundant now since offset needs to be tracked directly on the plane group.

Added a connect_perspective component to help with stuff that works off the perspective atom.

#### Misc

I read weather code while working on the plane master stuff here, and got a little upset about how it worked (we have to update every plane master when changing weather). So I changed it to use a holder vis contents (which plane masters "subscribe" to based off their z level) and then sticking the particles inside those holders. Mucked about with the code involved a little bit to make this work.

I may have missed some details, this is an older pr I was working on a few months ago that I'm just now finishing.


## Why It's Good For The Game


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f52d0876-9283-4e5e-aaae-23d064da7b25

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f706068-98dd-4e0a-835f-5bf8270d1aab

changes.text: Space parallax now works through cameras and other "external maps"
Cameras and friends will no longer be incorrectly culled/shrunk when displaying a z level other then your own.
Fucked with how space parallax/the renderer thinks about "where" it is being displayed pretty heavily. Please report any weird visuals!

title: Fangs: moves various pseudo-fangs to a new fang organ. Makes adjustments to relevant species.
author: necromanceranne
body:
## About The Pull Request

Creates a new fang organ that handles the effects of pseudo-fang tongues like cat tongues, vampire tongues, carp tongues and stout tongues. 

Any benefits to unarmed attacks or interactions (or, in the case of vampires, the entire blood sucking ability), is now attached to this fang organ.

Lizardpeople also get fangs.

Vampires and lizardpeople gain a trait called TRAIT_REFINED_BITER, which causes the holder to sometimes bit in place of an unarmed attack, unlike feral biters, who will always bite.

Adds cybernetic fangs, which are unlocked via the Cybernetics tech node, at the same time as advanced limbs.

## Why It's Good For The Game

I got really annoyed by the way fangs and sharp teeth were handled as tongues, so we're separating these out entirely into their own bespoke organ. Also means you can separate out changing your tongue from changing your fangs without any problems.

I like biting.

changes.text: Fangs, which now handle the functionality of pseudo-fang tongues. Felinids, lizardpeople, vampires, carp-infused and stout-infused people now have their own fangs.
Vampire fangs now handle all vampire blood-draining effects.
Cybernetic fangs, unlocked via the Cybernetics tech node.

title: Damage procs, physiology and damage_coeff refactor.
author: Ghommie
body:
## About The Pull Request
I've decided that refactoring physiology would be a good thing to do. I didn't like seeing the amount of typechecking that it previously required, and the fact that it was basically just a holder datum and nothing more wasn't particularly great either.

It also turns out there was also the damage_coeff list that simple_animal and basic mobs use that fulfilled a similar role, so I had to refactor it as well, meaning everything would have to go straight to `living_defines.dm`...

And that devolved a relatively small refactor into something more radical and a lot of damage procs were reworked a bit as well. **Fun fact: physiology didn't cover adjust_brute/burn/tox/oxy/stamina_loss procs and only apply_damage() before, now it does.**

## Why It's Good For The Game

Less typechecking and a more flexible solution for damage as well as other coefficients that can be applied to all mobs. These are mainly backend changes but some of them may be perceived on the front as well. See the **bold** text above.

changes.text: Refactored the code for damage and types of damage a little (also armor but not as much). Make sure to report any oddity with it.

title: Adds Subtle Gender Indicating Tooltips to Speaker Names in Chat
author: JohnFulpWillard
body:

title: Head revolutionaries can set a "conversion guideline"
author: MrMelbert
body: ## About The Pull Request In their antag info UI, headrevs can set a "conversion guideline". This guideline is sent to people they convert as a part of their greet, it looks like this (wording not final): Current wording: ``` A directive echoes through your mind... [guideline_text] This is a guideline instilled upon you from your (new) leader - while you are expected to follow it where possible, it is not a strict order. Further orders from your (new) leader(s) may supersede this. ``` ## Why It's Good For The Game Right now if you want to do something gimmicky as a head revolutionary, you really have to take it slow - Find someone alone, flash, shake them awake, explain your plan, repeat... This process is makes an already difficult antagonist a ton more difficult for people who want to do something atypical (i.e. not flashing as many people as possible and rushing the heads of staff) With the guideline message, these people who want to do something different now have the ability to give their revs the cliff notes of what they're trying to do, though more complicated plans would still require you tell them in person. For example you could set a guideline like "Remove security's mindshields and revive them" to indicate you want to try to kill as few people as possible. At the end of the day I phrased it as a *guideline*, rather than a strict order, to keep revolutionaries from being stuck following some benign order until they all get deconverted or die. I didn't want revolutionaries ordered to "be pacifists" to get in trouble for fighting someone in self-defense.

changes.text: Head revolutionaries can set a "conversion guideline" - a short message sent to all people they convert - in their antag ui, to help them bring some order to the revolution. It is, however, ultimately a *guideline*. You're note forced to follow it but are expected to abide by it .

title: Removes spear breaking
author: necromanceranne
body:
## About The Pull Request

Entirely removes spear breaking mechanics.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Wasn't really as good a limitation as I thought, and mostly just pissed people off. People don't actually use spears against people as much as you'd think, which is a shame. Hell, people don't even use it for the reach. They should, but I can't make people use it. One for the folk in the know I guess.

But as a consequence, this predominantly hurt their functionality when used to break objects. And people more often used them to break objects. (ignore that it has a demolish malice, people do not see the numbers). Which usually has more integrity than a single spear.

So generally speaking, giving spears 'pseudo-ammo' was mostly just a colossal pain in the ass for their most common use, and may have also just actively discouraged their use as weapons further.

changes.text: Spears no longer break from overuse without repair.
